summary: Aermotor tower erected 1932 by the Wisconsin Conservation Commission at a site about 2.5 miles away, moved by CCC to its present Oconto County site in 1935; open to climb May to November.

facts.design: Galvanized steel Aermotor LS-40 tower on four concrete piers, about 100 ft tall, with a 7x7-ft cab

staffing.status: no longer used as a fire lookout; open to visitors

access.note: Open May 1 to November 1, daily 8 a.m. to sunset; visitors may climb to the top. Forest Service site.

visit.trail_note: Gravel road runs uphill to a parking area just north of the tower; visitors climb the stairs to the cab

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest, Lakewood-Laona Ranger District)

events.note: Prefabricated by Aermotor in 1932 and erected by the Wisconsin Conservation Commission at its original site about two and a half miles away; pier dated 10/22/32
CCC crews dismantled the tower and are believed to have rebuilt it at its present site; Forest Service bought the site 17 January 1935
Former CCC enrollee Marvin P. Heisler recalled staffing the tower in 1940
Last fire called in from the tower, 25 April 1970
Radio antenna and relay shelter added by the Oconto County City Ambulance and Law Enforcement Committee; both removed 1993 or 1994
Rehabilitated as an interpretive site 1993-94: deteriorated wooden components replaced, steel bracing and rails added, six interpretive panels placed
Added to the National Register of Historic Places August 19, 2008 (ref. 08000790)
Restored 2015-16 with financial help from the Oconto County Economic Development Corporation and more than 500 hours of Forest Service employee work

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2008 nomination dates the Aermotor prefabrication and first erection to 1932 (pier dated 10/22/32 at the original site) and the relocation to 1935. The Forest Service page and Wikipedia date the build to 1935. The story gives 1932 for the first erection and 1935 for the move; the brief's 1932 is kept.

The Forest Service calls it the first Wisconsin lookout on both the NHLR and the NRHP. The NPS record and Wikipedia put the Fifield tower's NRHP listing in 2007, a year before this tower's 2008 listing. The story reports the forest's claim and notes the NRHP date.
The register says it is the only remaining lookout on the forest; the nomination says it is one of two remaining of the original 19. The story reports both as the sources' own words.
